title: Degree-two characteristic-p vanishing for arbitrary constant coefficients
statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field of prime characteristic p, Λ any commutative ring, and f : C → Spec k a smooth separated connected scheme of finite type and dimension at most one [def-sc-curves]. The degree-two Ext cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] of the underlying abelian sheaf of the constant Λ-module sheaf Λ/pΛ [def-sc-constant-sheaves] is zero. No finiteness or characteristic hypothesis on Λ is imposed.

proof.text: In dimension zero, smooth finite-type connected C over algebraically closed k is Spec k. Choose the geometric point over k and apply zero-dimensional-etale-cohomology-rest in degree two to the underlying abelian sheaf. The Ext/derived comparison transfers this vanishing to Sheaf.H.

In dimension one C is an IsConnectedCurve. Artin–Schreier gives zero degree-two derived cohomology of the constant ZMod p sheaf. The natural Ext/derived comparison gives the same vanishing for Sheaf.H.

The additive group Λ/pΛ is an F_p-vector space. It is the filtered colimit, indexed in the coefficient universe, of its finite-dimensional subspaces. Each is a finite sum of ZMod p. Constant sheafification and coefficient forgetting preserve this colimit, and additive cohomology vanishes on the finite sums. The large filtered-colimit continuity theorem on the qcqs curve then gives zero degree-two cohomology for Λ/pΛ. This includes the zero quotient and infinite-dimensional quotients.

proof_origin.place: C3 proof, with explicit coefficient extension by finite-dimensional subspaces and dimension-zero case
